basics.description: Global Profile Page: a self-service account page for users of Azure AD B2C or Entra External ID, running on Azure Container Apps.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Region of the Container Apps environment and the other regional resources.

basics.name: name
basics.label: Workload name

constraints.validationMessage: Use 3 to 12 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen.

basics.toolTip: Used in every resource name after the Microsoft abbreviation of its type (ca-, cae-, kv-, st, id-, log-...). 3 to 12 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.

options.text: The image of this version is filled in. Enter the registry token name and password you received from LinkCode. They are used once, to copy the image into a registry the deployment creates for you, and are not stored.

elements.name: containerImage
elements.label: Image

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a full image reference: registry/repository:tag.

elements.toolTip: Change it only to deploy another version. The image is copied into this deployment's own registry.

elements.name: registryUsername
elements.label: Registry token name

constraints.validationMessage: The token name, for example contoso-prod: 5 to 50 letters, digits or hyphens. The password goes in the next field.

elements.toolTip: The short token name from LinkCode, not the password. Empty only for a public image.

elements.name: registryPassword
elements.toolTip: The long token password from LinkCode.

elements.name: identityProvider
elements.label: Identity provider
elements.toolTip: Entra External ID for a new customer tenant; Azure AD B2C for an existing B2C tenant.

elements.name: tenantName
elements.label: Tenant name

constraints.validationMessage: Enter the part before .onmicrosoft.com, in lowercase.

elements.toolTip: For example contoso for contoso.onmicrosoft.com. The sign-in host (contoso.b2clogin.com or contoso.ciamlogin.com) is derived from it.

elements.name: registrations
elements.label: App registrations
elements.toolTip: Recommended: after the deployment a tenant administrator opens the setupUrl output, enters setupCode and signs in once (LinkCode setup app); the app creates its registrations, permissions and the B2C ROPC flow itself and keeps their secrets in Key Vault.

options.text: After the deployment, open the setupUrl output and enter setupCode. Sign in there as a Global Administrator of the B2C or External ID tenant, and accept the permissions of LinkCode setup; setup takes about two minutes and restarts the app.

elements.name: azureAdTenantId
elements.label: Tenant id
elements.toolTip: Directory (tenant) id of the identity provider tenant.

elements.name: azureAdClientId
elements.label: Client id
elements.toolTip: App registration with redirect URI https://<app host>/signin-oidc (add it after the deployment, the app host is shown in the outputs). It also calls Microsoft Graph unless you choose a separate registration in the next step.

elements.name: azureAdClientSecret
elements.toolTip: A client secret of the web sign-in app registration. Stored in Key Vault.

elements.name: azureAdSignUpSignInPolicyId
elements.label: Sign-up/sign-in policy

constraints.validationMessage: A B2C user flow (B2C_1_…) or custom policy (B2C_1A_…).

elements.toolTip: A user flow (B2C_1_…) or custom policy (B2C_1A_…). With /setup, a built-in user flow that does not exist yet is created.

elements.name: userFlow
elements.label: User flow (optional)
elements.toolTip: Entra External ID: name of the sign-up and sign-in user flow /setup adds the app to. Empty: add the app to a flow in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

constraints.validationMessage: Letters, digits, spaces, underscores, hyphens and dots only.

options.text: The registration that calls Microsoft Graph needs the application permissions User.ReadWrite.All, UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All and AuditLog.Read.All (and Application.Read.All when the My Apps page is on), with admin consent.

elements.name: useSignInRegistration
elements.label: Registration for Microsoft Graph
elements.toolTip: One registration is enough for sign-in and Microsoft Graph. Choose a separate one only if your policy requires it.

elements.name: graphClientId
elements.label: Client id
elements.toolTip: Application (client) id of the registration with the Microsoft Graph application permissions.

elements.name: graphClientSecret
elements.toolTip: A client secret of that registration. Stored in Key Vault.

elements.name: ropcPolicyId
elements.label: ROPC user flow

constraints.validationMessage: A B2C user flow (B2C_1_…) or custom policy (B2C_1A_…).

elements.toolTip: B2C only: the user flow (resource owner password credentials) that checks the current password before a password change. With /setup, a missing built-in flow is created.

elements.name: ropcClientId
elements.label: ROPC client id
elements.toolTip: B2C only: public client registration used with the ROPC user flow.

elements.name: stepUpRequiredClaimValue
elements.label: Step-up required claim value
elements.toolTip: Empty: step-up authentication is off.

elements.name: stepUpClaimType
elements.label: Step-up claim type

constraints.validationMessage: A claim name, for example acr.

elements.toolTip: The claim in the token that carries the step-up value, usually acr.

elements.name: stepUpB2CPolicy
elements.label: Step-up B2C policy

constraints.validationMessage: A B2C user flow (B2C_1_…) or custom policy (B2C_1A_…).

elements.toolTip: B2C only: the user flow or custom policy that performs the step-up (multi-factor) sign-in.

elements.name: stepUpAuthenticationContextId
elements.label: Step-up authentication context id

constraints.validationMessage: An authentication context id, c1 to c99.

elements.toolTip: Entra External ID: Conditional Access authentication context, for example c1.

elements.name: googleClientId
elements.label: Google client id

constraints.validationMessage: A Google OAuth client id, ending with .apps.googleusercontent.com.

elements.toolTip: Turns Google account linking on. Redirect URI: https://<app host>/bff/link/google/callback.

elements.name: googleClientSecret
elements.toolTip: The client secret of the Google OAuth client. Stored in Key Vault.

elements.name: enableVerificationCodes
elements.label: Add e-mail or phone with a code
elements.toolTip: Lets users add an e-mail address (and, with an SMS sender, a phone number) as a sign-in method after confirming a one-time code. The codes are sent by Azure Communication Services, which the deployment creates. Off: no Communication Services resources, and the Security page does not offer adding these methods. Sign-in, sign-up and password reset e-mails are sent by the identity provider and are not affected.

elements.name: smsSenderType
elements.label: SMS sender
elements.toolTip: Phone verification sends codes from Azure Communication Services. A phone number has a monthly fee; an alphanumeric sender ID (for example the company name) has none but must be enabled in ACS and is only supported in some countries, Poland included. Recipients cannot reply to it.

elements.name: smsSenderNumber
elements.label: SMS sender number

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a number in E.164 format, for example +48123456789.

elements.toolTip: Phone number bought in Azure Communication Services.

elements.name: smsSenderId
elements.label: SMS sender ID

constraints.validationMessage: Use 1-11 letters, digits or spaces, with at least one letter, for example CIS.

elements.toolTip: Alphanumeric sender ID enabled in Azure Communication Services (Phone numbers, Alphanumeric sender ID).

elements.name: signInActivitySource
elements.label: Sign-in history
elements.toolTip: Microsoft Graph: the Recent activity page reads the tenant sign-in log on demand (B2C keeps 7 days). Event Hub: creates an event hub for the tenant Diagnostic settings and keeps sign-ins in the app's own table (Event Hubs Standard costs extra). After deployment, create the Diagnostic setting in the tenant as described in docs/sign-in-activity.md.

elements.name: signInRetentionDays
elements.label: Sign-in history retention (days)
elements.toolTip: How long sign-ins are kept in the app's own table.

elements.name: enableMyApps
elements.label: My Apps page
elements.toolTip: Shows users the applications they signed in to, built from the sign-in history (with Microsoft Graph as the source only the last 7 days in B2C or 30 days in External ID). Needs the Microsoft Graph application permission Application.Read.All on the Graph app registration, to read app names, logos and links.

elements.name: myAppsSource
elements.label: My Apps source
elements.toolTip: Token issuances: the B2C audit log's 'Issue an id_token to the application' events, which name the app the user signed in to (with the Event Hub sign-in history, also stream AuditLogs, docs/my-apps.md). Sign-in history: apps exactly as the sign-in log records them (with B2C custom policies every sign-in is ProxyIdentityExperienceFramework).

elements.name: redisMode
elements.label: Redis cache
elements.toolTip: Azure Managed Redis shares verification codes and token caches between replicas. Without it the app runs as one replica and pending codes are lost on restart or scale to zero.

elements.name: minReplicas
elements.label: Minimum replicas
elements.toolTip: 0 scales to zero when idle: cheapest, with a cold start of a few seconds on the next request.

elements.name: maxReplicas
elements.label: Maximum replicas
elements.toolTip: Upper limit for scaling out under load. Only with Redis.
